newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan said the agenda of Tuesday's Social Affairs Council would be based mainly on the adoption of the directive on posting of workers COM(91)230 and Commissioner Flynn's information to the Council on information and consultation of workers COM(95)547 launched in November 1995.

She said there was some resistance, especially by Germany which did not want a formula that would lead to the watering down of the employee participation clauses. She said that in order to solve the German problem, the issue would be studied by a group of experts.

Nolan also said consultation had shown that a majority of member states were in favor of an European approach to the issue of information and consultation in national undertakings. Therefore, she said, the Commission would pursue a consultation under the social agreement to see if they can come up with an agreement on this subject.
In answer to a question, Nolan said the Commission was working on a green paper on the reduction of working hours.

Spokesman Patrick Child briefed on the informal ECOFIN Council held on Saturday in Dublin to discuss EMU. He said the Council decided to continue works towards a reinforced convergence system. On the legal framework of the Euro, Child said Art. 109 L.4 of the Maastricht Treaty would be used as legal basis.

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the trans-European networks would be formally discussed during the ECOFIN Council of October 14. Van der Pas said ten member states were in favour of supplementary financing. He added that Commission President Jacques Santer would insist that coherence should be kept in the EU budget. Van der Pass said that if money was refused in one sector because no room for manoeuvre could be found in the budget, it was surprising to see huge amounts unblocked for another sector only few days later.
Van der Pas added that if supplementary funds were not found for trans-European networks, there was a risk that the European Parliament would block money already available in this sector.

Asked about the Lome Convention, spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the state of ratification was still very poor and that there would be no project started before two thirds of the ACP countries and the 15 member states ratified the convention.

Spokesman Peter Guilford said member states had not yet reached a fully united position on labor standards as one member state did not believe the World Trade Organisation was the right forum for the issue.
Asked about press reports implying the Commission would have blocked a 78 million Ecu loan to a South-African company, spokesman Child denied the Commission had considered such a decision.
The Commission released the following documents:
- Speech/96/221: Speech of Commissioner Pinheiro at the ACP-EC Assembly.
